import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Since df is already loaded, I'll verify its structure and compute group totals
print("DataFrame shape:", df.shape)
print("
Column data types:")
print(df.dtypes)

# Identify categorical columns for grouping
categorical_cols = df.select_dtypes(include=['object', 'category']).columns.tolist()
print("
Categorical columns (potential grouping variables):")
print(categorical_cols)

# Choose a few key categorical columns for grouping analysis
# Based on the data, likely 'customer_segment', 'customer_tier', 'lifecycle_stage', etc.
grouping_cols = ['customer_segment', 'customer_tier', 'lifecycle_stage']

# Compute per-group totals for estimated_customer_ltv
group_totals = df.groupby(grouping_cols)['estimated_customer_ltv'].sum().reset_index()
group_totals = group_totals.sort_values('estimated_customer_ltv', ascending=False)
print("
Per-group totals of estimated_customer_ltv (top 20 groups):")
print(group_totals.head(20))

# If "running totals" refers to cumulative sums, we can compute that as well
group_totals['cumulative_total'] = group_totals['estimated_customer_ltv'].cumsum()
group_totals['percentage_of_total'] = (group_totals['estimated_customer_ltv'] / group_totals['estimated_customer_ltv'].sum()) * 100
print("
Group totals with cumulative sums and percentages:")
print(group_totals.head(10))
